reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an instructional tour of Oracle, a StocksToTrade watchlist-building and stock-trade prediction tool, with the speaker demonstrating trading-interface screens. The request to sign up is described as an ordinary commercial promotion tied to the demonstrated tool, without payment terms, account-data collection, deceptive destination behavior, or a deceptive participation flow. The speaker also qualifies that identified stocks are not necessarily trades or certain outcomes.

it takes the market data at the open as well as pre market data, compiles that, and builds your a list of potential entries, and support, and resistance levels
Sign up for StocksToTrade at https://orders.stockstotrade.com

opening.argument: The presentation links a requested sign-up to a tool marketed for identifying trades and guiding entry decisions. The description calls Oracle “amazing” for traders building stock lists and plans, then directs viewers to sign up for StocksToTrade. The speaker also presents the product as a prediction algorithm that finds stocks with potential movement and offers potential entries. This is not merely abstract market education: the requested action is connected to using a trading system intended to shape actual trades.

citations.quote: Oracle is amazing for busy traders looking to build a list of stocks as well as create plans based on technical support and resistance levels.
Sign up for StocksToTrade at https://orders.stockstotrade.com
oracle is our watchlist building as well as stock trade prediction algorithm
builds your a list of potential entries, and support, and resistance levels

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video an introduction does not remove the commercial action it asks viewers to take. The sign-up link appears alongside claims that the system helps create trading plans, while the demonstration supplies concrete signal levels and trade examples. Saying entries are “potential” qualifies certainty, but it still connects the product to decisions involving real market positions.

I would look to buy this stock at this breakthrough of this 138 level
I would probably have a profit goal of 173 plus.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence shows a tutorial and a conventional product invitation, not a promise that users will receive returns. The speaker expressly says the tool is only a tool and that identified stocks are not necessarily trades. A suggested buy level and personal profit goal describe an example trading plan, not guaranteed performance or a required deployment of funds.

opening.argument: Several risk signals are concentrated in the same pitch: a proprietary prediction algorithm, claims that it finds stocks with the most potential to move, real-time entry and stop levels, and a stated profit goal. The speaker describes Oracle as useful for new and busy traders, while the description calls it “amazing” and provides a direct sign-up URL. Even with cautionary wording, this combination can make speculative trading appear systematized and actionable, encouraging viewers to rely on a branded algorithm for profit-seeking decisions.

citations.quote: it builds a list of stocks that have the most potential to move on the day.
it predicts based on our proprietary algorithm
I would probably have a profit goal of 173 plus.
Sign up for StocksToTrade at https://orders.stockstotrade.com

rebuttal.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the overall impression created by repeated references to prediction, potential breakouts, and profit targets. “Proprietary” means viewers cannot assess the method from this material, yet the presentation still frames its outputs as useful for deciding when to buy, short, or stop out. The commercial link makes those risk signals consequential.

citations.quote: it predicts based on our proprietary algorithm
I would look to buy this stock at this breakthrough of this 138 level
I have a stop back here at the long trigger of 5.87

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are visibly presented as indicators and possible scenarios, not easy or assured returns. The speaker repeatedly limits the claims, including that the tool is only a guideline and that a stock may merely be a potential trade. A proprietary calculation and a sign-up URL do not, by themselves, establish deceptive returns or a required trading workflow.

opening.argument: Although framed as education, the video functions as product promotion. It identifies the presenter with StocksToTrade, repeatedly describes Oracle as especially useful for new, intermediate, and busy traders, demonstrates its trading signals and levels, and ends with a sign-up pathway. The instructional format therefore serves to make a speculative trading product appear practical and ready for use. The examples do not merely explain terminology; they show how to turn the displayed signals into entries, stops, and a profit objective.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes the screen tour but omits how the tour steers use of the product. The speaker explains when he would short, where he would stop out, and where he would seek profit, while the description calls the tool “amazing” and directs viewers to sign up. That is promotional guidance embedded in instruction, not a neutral explanation detached from participation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An instructional demonstration can include a commercial sign-up without becoming a scam. The content explains interface mechanics, support and resistance, and limitations; it does not promise that viewers will earn money, require deposits, or claim that the examples will succeed. The speaker even describes the output as a template to potentially guide a trade, leaving the decision with the viewer.
